findings.title: Failure checkpoint contradicts freeze semantics
findings.section: Requirements — R5 (failed-query frozen state) and R6 (acceptance bar)
findings.why_it_matters: A failed query can leave Skip deliberately displaying a stale last-good aggregate while an independent Convex reader observes newer source data, so R5 and R6 cannot both be satisfied at a query-failure checkpoint. This makes the stated semantic-correctness acceptance bar impossible for the failure scenario the plan explicitly chooses; limiting reader equality to recovery preserves the user-settled freeze behavior while still verifying convergence.
findings.suggested_fix: Revise R6 to require independent-Convex-reader equality at bootstrap, multi-table-update, unsubscribe, reconnect, and post-recovery checkpoints; for the query-failure checkpoint, require retention of the last successful aggregate plus a visible stale indicator, without asserting equality to the current independent reader.
evidence: R5: its previously-derived Skip view is retained (frozen at last-good) rather than cleared, and the demo surfaces that the value may be stale.

R6: At each controlled checkpoint ... the demo's Skip-derived aggregate matches an independent Convex reader across bootstrap, a multi-table update, query failure and recovery, unsubscribe, and reconnect with a fresh snapshot.

residual_risks: Chunk reassembly is demonstrated only with protocol fixtures; the document explicitly defers end-to-end transitions above the chunk threshold, so live framing behavior at that threshold remains unvalidated before any generalization decision.
deferred_questions: Planning must choose the pinned sync authentication mode, which determines the credential acquisition and connection setup exercised by the proof.
Planning must select the mechanism that makes each transition a single Skip update: one combined input domain or a narrowly scoped atomic multi-collection capability.

findings.title: Failure checkpoint contradicts freeze semantics
findings.section: Requirements — R5 (failed-query frozen state) and R6 (acceptance bar)
findings.consequence: The acceptance bar requires equality with current Convex state precisely when the settled decision deliberately preserves a stale last-good view, so the query-failure scenario cannot pass both rules.
findings.recommendation: Revise R6 as stated in the suggested correction; compare equality after recovery and test retained stale state separately at failure.
findings.suggested_correction: Revise R6 to require independent-reader equality at bootstrap, multi-table update, unsubscribe, reconnect, and post-recovery checkpoints; for failure, require last-good retention and a visible stale indicator without current-reader equality.
